messages:
ravi: quick q — need to disable the prod rerank rollout (flag: rerank_v2). Observing latency spikes on order paths. Who's allowed to flip the kill switch and what's the emergency flow? tagging oncall: @tara

tara_oncall: I can flip this. Quick checklist before I do: 1) confirm impact and scope, 2) flip flag, 3) notify #incidents + support, 4) create incident record, 5) capture audit/event id. If you confirm impact, say 'go' and I'll act.

eli_sre: perms/ownership: SRE oncall + platform leads have the "feature-toggle-admin" role. Two ways to flip: console (flags.redwood.internal) or API. API example (will generate an audit event automatically):
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/rerank_v2' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"state":"off","meta":{"reason":"latency spike","incident":"INC-2026-045"}}'
```
This call writes an immutable audit entry and emits an event to the flags event stream (used by dashboards/alerts).

jules_pm: question: when you flip, do we set to 0%/off globally or do a canary rollback? my preference is to scope to the least-impacting audience, but if latency is system-wide, global off is OK. Also add the reason and incident id in the meta so support+CS can read it.

mike_staff: if traffic is severely degraded, global off is fine — we can re-enable in batches later. alternative: dynamic routing -> point the prod audience to rerank_v1 variant while keeping flag on for canary orgs. Example route change is in the routing console, not the flag API.

deploy-bot: [system] flag.rerank_v2 change requested by tara_oncall — awaiting execution/approval.

ravi: impact confirmed from monitoring: 12% latency p95 jump on order flow starting 14:02 UTC. go from product: @jules says do global off for now.

tara_oncall: executing now via API. pasting command and response:
```bash
curl -X POST 'https://flags.internal.redwood/api/v1/flags/rerank_v2' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"state":"off","meta":{"reason":"prod-latency","incident":"INC-2026-045","acted_by":"tara_oncall"}}'
```
response: 200 OK
event_id: EVT-9876
audit_link: https://logs.redwood.internal/audit/EVT-9876
:white_check_mark: flipped to OFF, routing reverted to rerank_v1 for all prod traffic. Notifying #incidents and paging list now.

ravi: thanks — can you also paste the list of affected customers/segments so SRE+support can prioritize outreach?

eli_sre: use this query on the request logs dashboard (Grafana link):
```sql
select customer_id, count(*) as calls
from prod.requests
where route like '%/orders%' and model = 'rerank_v2' and ts >= '2026-03-17T14:00:00Z'
group by customer_id
order by calls desc
```
That will show top impacted customers.

tara_oncall: alerted support (@support) and product (@jules). Escalation path in case of data concerns: SRE lead -> Eng Director -> CISO. For standard perf incidents, SRE + PM + Support is the chain. Also: save the incident timeline in the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-045

jules_pm: noted. We'll hold the rollout, block any new canaries, and schedule a postmortem tomorrow. Thanks for quick action.

mike_staff: follow-up guardrails: add a temporary automation rule to block rerank_v2 re-enables without a REQUIRED_TAG = "postmortem:INC-2026-045". Also create a short-lived alert that fires if p95 goes up after re-enable.

tara_oncall: done — created flag lock (requires "postmortem" tag to override). Audit events: EVT-9876 (off) and EVT-9877 (lock). If anyone needs the CLI steps or keys, ping me.

ravi: appreciate it. cc @customer-success for outreach.

jules_pm: :thumbsup: we'll own comms. schedule follow-up sync in 1hr.
